claims.text: Creep in nanoscale FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is governed by stress-assisted dislocation climb.
Coherent multilayer interfaces facilitate stress-assisted dislocation climb.
Local chemical short-range order and lattice distortion alter local diffusion kinetics and barriers to dislocation motion.
The proposed initial coating has alternating FCC and BCC HEA layers with coherent interfaces and a relatively chemically disordered as-deposited state.
Controlled pre-annealing can increase SRO while otherwise preserving identical samples.
Temperatures above approximately 500 °C place the proposed multilayer in an applicable creep regime.
The local structure, chemistry, SRO, and lattice distortion of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces mediate diffusion pathways and dislocation climb.
Under sustained high-temperature loading, dislocations accumulate at the layer interfaces.
Chemical SRO and severe lattice distortion reduce the energy barrier for dislocation climb by enhancing lattice diffusion.
Diffusion-assisted climb allows dislocations to bypass interface obstacles and thereby produces progressive creep deformation.
Enhanced SRO will produce a higher creep strain rate than the as-deposited baseline.
Enhanced SRO will produce more pronounced dislocation-climb activity at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Progressive deformation will be accompanied by increased dislocation density and interface slip localized in regions of high SRO.
As-deposited HEA multilayers have a random elemental distribution and minimal SRO.
The as-deposited baseline will have lower creep rate and dislocation activity under identical loading.
The proposed mechanism is limited to conditions in which the nanoscale multilayer architecture and constituent phase stability are retained.
Sufficient ordering can alter phase constitution or promote secondary ordered phases, potentially invalidating the proposed mechanism.

A failure of enhanced-SRO samples to show a statistically significant increase in creep rate and interface climb activity, or a failure to find correlation between SRO and interface deformation, would falsify the hypothesis.
